gamma_ray.fact_ray: 14 facts: 14 π Moderate. Each is written beside its evidence above.

configs.what: The firewall and its recommended allowlist are on.
Model Context Protocol servers and other applications.

facts.label: It executes actions itself
facts.fact: It "can create branches, write code, and open pull requests in response to assigned issues".

facts.label: The agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only
facts.fact: It picks up a task, creates a branch, writes code and opens a pull request on its own, pushing only to the existing pull request branch when triggered by mention or otherwise to a new copilot/ branch; Actions workflows its pull requests trigger need approval from a user with write access before they run. The credit rests on that workflow-approval gate plus the pull-request flow; no sentence on the page states which decisions the person must approve.
facts.quote: require approval from a user with write access before they will run

facts.label: It connects to external tools or services across a trust boundary
facts.fact: Repository-level MCP servers connect it to external tools; by default only the GitHub server (read-only token on the current repository) and a Playwright server limited to localhost are configured.
facts.quote: GitHub.com supports MCP servers configured at the repository level

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: Workflows triggered by its pull requests "require approval from a user with write access before they will run".
facts.quote: require approval from a user with write access before they will run

facts.label: What it can reach is enumerated: scopes, permissions, tools
facts.fact: The vendor documents its permission scopes: read-only where the user has only read access, one branch to push to, and only the secrets and variables added to the copilot environment.
facts.quote: Copilot is read-only when a user has read access

facts.label: Its purpose and permitted tasks are stated in writing
facts.fact: The vendor states intended uses: maintenance, feature development, prototyping.

facts.label: Its limits and known failure cases are documented for those who use it
facts.fact: The page lists limitations: limited scope, inaccurate code, security risks, public code matches.

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of GitHub's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
